speaker: SPEAKER_00
transcript: Well, Senator Roberts and I are working closely together to find a way forward on reauthorizing the child nutrition law, the five-year bill, and I'm hopeful we're going to be able to do that. The great news is that 97% of our schools are now in compliance with the Healthy Food Standards. And we have been providing flexibility on whole grains and sodium the last couple of years through the appropriations process. And certainly we want to continue to support schools and give them flexibility. But we also know now that because of terrific leadership at the local level. schools now are working not only with healthy food standards, but I'm very excited about the efforts on farm to school and school gardens. I think one of the most fun things for me to do is to go out to a school and have them walk me through the garden and have the students talk about what they have been growing and all of the things related to that. It's such a terrific learning process and they're much more excited about eating fresh fruits and vegetables if they've grown them. So there's a lot of things that were in this five-year bill that are really starting to take hold. So we don't want to go backwards. We want to go forwards. And the other thing that I'm very concerned about is that we only have about 18% of the children who are getting school meals, low-income children who are eating during the school year. that are able to get healthy meals in the summer, 18%. And so that is clearly not acceptable in our great country. And as the generals have said to us, you know, we need healthy young people that can step up and qualify and serve our country and the armed services. And we hear from the medical community about health care costs, the $14 billion a year we're spending and obesity and other health risk diseases that relate to lack of good nutrition for children. So we can do better than that and I believe that we can keep moving forward and that's what we're working on.
